event: You stack the empty cartons.
One dumpling is left in the near carton, marooned by politeness, and you rescue it.
You cut it into three even pieces with the edge of the fork.
Nova takes her third off your fingers, chin still on your shoulder.
She doesn't eat it right away; her eyes cut to the fort and back.
Whatever crosses her face gets folded under the next, loud thing she says.
"Okay. Fort motion." Non-negotiable, but called a motion so it stays polite.
She peels off your side, one hand out for you and one for Astra.
"Everybody in. I built the thing. Come see what it's for."
Astra doesn't take the hand yet; she looks at the shelf, once, quick.
Then she takes the hand, and Nova hauls, never once gently.
The three of you go down into the fort in a slow avalanche of paperbacks and elbows.
Inside is warmer; the good blanket from the couch is down over its floor.
Lamplight comes through the paperback walls in thin gold seams.
There's exactly enough room for three if two of them overlap.
You end up on your back.
Astra fits along one side of you without being asked.
Nova stakes the other, propped on an elbow over your chest, lipstick close now.
"From in here," Astra says quietly, "it's better." She doesn't say better than what.
You find a hand at the small of Nova's back and keep it there.
"Okay. Show me what it's for."
Nova reaches over your shoulder into the deep seam where the blanket meets the wall.
Her hand closes on something that's waited there since before dinner.
She holds it where it is and looks at you, at her fist, at you again.
She opens her mouth, and closes it again.
Out of the fist comes a wrecked paperback, its spine gone white and soft.
The cover is a cheap dragon worn almost featureless, the book swollen with rereading.
She sets it on your sternum like it weighs more than it does.
You lay a hand flat over it.
"Okay, so, don't," she says fast, hands up: don't do a face.
It's the first one she ever— she stops, and comes back lower.
She was fourteen; the prose is genuinely bad and eleven rereads haven't improved it.
Astra comes up on an elbow on your other side to see.
She doesn't reach for the book; she reads the margins from where she is.
Pen crowds every white edge in a kid's hand, cramped and sure.
The faint light under Astra's skin comes up, and she looks straight at you while it does.
"Read us the part," Astra says. "The one with the corner turned down."
Nova takes the book back in two careful hands and finds the page without hunting.
She doesn't do a voice: no goblin delivery, no bit.
She reads low and plain, as a thing known by heart, the loud machine of her gone quiet.

memory.fact: Nova goes dead still when something absorbs her.

event: It's not good prose; she was right about that.
A boy on a wall at the end of everything, holding a sword he can't use, deciding to stay.
Earnest and overwritten, plainly the most important thing that ever happened to somebody.
She reads it like it still is.
Astra doesn't move, her eyes on Nova's mouth and not the page, the glow still up.
Nova's thumb finds the margin and she stops reading aloud, book flat to her chest.
Her red eyes rest on the pen scrawl there; for a second nobody says anything.
"Fourteen-year-old me put a note here. I'm not reading you the note."
You get a hand into the short hair at the back of her neck.
"Okay," you say. "Not the note."
